title: Type with a point of view.
summary: Finding character in the tension between structure and individuality.
paragraphs: An exploration of typography as both identity and expression. Drawing on the elegance of Art Deco, the experimental spirit of the avant-garde and the timeless geometry of classical letterforms, this bespoke composition finds its character in the tension between structure and individuality.

Each letter is carefully considered, with unexpected curves, exaggerated proportions and unconventional relationships creating a distinctive visual rhythm. The result is a wordmark that feels simultaneously familiar and unfamiliar, balancing architectural precision with a playful disregard for convention.

More than an exercise in lettering, it captures something fundamental about Random Order itself: finding beauty in the unexpected, challenging established forms and allowing experimentation to give rise to an identity entirely its own.

title: A character to rally around.
summary: A tiger, a wordmark, a shared presence. Illustration gives an identity something to gather around.
paragraphs: The Team EARNT tiger does more than fill a space. Its bold silhouette and graphic wordmark give the composition an immediate centre of attention. The character is the first thing you read; the name follows.

Set beside Hally’s tangle of everyday moments, it suggests two different ways an illustration can shape an identity. One concentrates the energy into a single character. The other lets a whole world unfold.
These are different visual languages, connected by a simple question: what makes a brand recognisable before you read its name?
source: Editorial observation of existing Work A and Magazine artwork; no outcome claims

title: The box as a surface.
alt: Sneaker LAB × BSTN packaging with basketball court artwork
summary: Basketball, streetwear and sneaker care meet on one surface.
paragraphs: A court is already a graphic system: boundaries, circles, lines and blocks of colour. In the Sneaker LAB × BSTN packaging concept, that language becomes a way to bring basketball culture into the object itself.
The image and the package can be read together. The artwork provides the atmosphere; the edges of the box give it a physical frame. The surface becomes part of the story.

Follow that relationship into the Adidas project, where Johannesburg imagery and graphic typography meet on a wearable canvas. The format changes, but the conversation between image and object continues.
source: Existing Magazine summary and Work A visual descriptions; editorial interpretation
